question.problem:
Select the missing parts in a particular solution of the differential equation ${y}^{″}+36y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $6$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{3(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).
$$

*Hint: You may assume that the free term and all the sine coefficients in the Fourier series of the particular solution are equal to zero.*

The Fourier series of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-1}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})
$$
question.worked_solution:
We assume that a solution of our equation has the following Fourier series:

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).
$$

Now, we compute the derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}\frac{n\pi }{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}) \\ {y}_{p}^{″} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}\frac{n\pi }{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}\frac{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{p}^{″}$ and ${y}_{p}$ into the equation and have

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}\frac{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})+36({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}))={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{3(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).
$$

Rearranging the terms to find a common denominator:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}(36-\frac{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{9})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{3(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})
$$

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}(\frac{324-{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{9})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{3(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).
$$

Now, equating the cosine coefficients:

$$
\frac{{a}_{n}(324-{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2})}{9}=\frac{3(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}}\,⇒\,{a}_{n}=\frac{27(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}(324-{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2})}.
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{27(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}(324-{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2})}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).
$$
